---
title: "Rules of the Carapace"
---

::: {.quest-dialog}
**Prerequisites:** the Shield of Undo, and either companion from the Kennel. **Objective:** write permission rules that hold, and know where they stop holding.
**Time:** about 20 minutes. <span class="ao-badge">Last verified (docs, not run): Claude Code v2.1.323 and OpenCode v2.3.0 on 2026-11-13 (sources in `research/kennel-and-crypt.md`).</span>
:::

Rules are enforced by the **tool**, not the model. A line in your instructions file (such as `CLAUDE.md`) asking the agent to avoid something is guidance, and it does not change what is allowed.

Sort every action into three bins: **allow** (safe and routine), **ask** (you want to decide each time), **deny** (never).

::: {.panel-tabset group="companion"}

## Claude Code

Rules live in a settings file, as `Tool(specifier)`:

```json
{
  "permissions": {
    "allow": ["Bash(git status)", "Bash(pytest *)"],
    "ask":   ["Bash(git push *)"],
    "deny":  ["Read(./.env)", "Read(./.env.*)"]
  }
}
```

| File | Who it affects |
|---|---|
| `~/.claude/settings.json` | all your projects |
| `.claude/settings.json` | everyone on the project, if you commit it |
| `.claude/settings.local.json` | only you, in this project |

A deny from any file beats an allow from any file. A space before the `*` matters: `Bash(ls *)` matches `ls -la` but not `lsof`. There is no `.claudeignore` that restricts access. Use `Read(...)` deny rules.

## OpenCode

Rules are an ordered array and the **last match wins**:

```json
{
  "permissions": [
    { "action": "*", "resource": "*", "effect": "ask" },
    { "action": "shell", "resource": "git status *", "effect": "allow" },
    { "action": "shell", "resource": "git push *", "effect": "deny" }
  ]
}
```

Start with the ask-everything rule, then narrow, then put denies last.

:::

## Where the carapace has gaps

- Rules that match command **arguments** are fragile: `Bash(rm *)` does not match `/bin/rm` or `bash -c 'rm ...'`.
- Claude Code's sandbox is off by default. When on, it limits **shell commands only**; file tools, MCP servers and hooks run outside it, and by default it can still read `~/.ssh`.
- Your secrets in environment variables are inherited by the commands it runs.

Treat rules as one layer. Git (the Shield) and a throwaway folder are the others.
